content:
Apple today announced quarterly results, setting a third-quarter record and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Along with the earnings report, the company also stated that it now has more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions.

Apple now has 1.5 billion subscriptions, growing from 1 billion subscriptions reached three years ago.

Apple's services division is highly profitable and continues to grow steadily, with quarterly revenue increasing 12% to over US$30 billion...Apple emphasised that advertising, the App Store, AppleCare, Music, Video, cloud services and payment services all recorded growth. Cook stated that Apple has 1.5 billion paid subscriptions, including iCloud and subscriptions to apps on the App Store from which Apple can take a commission.

As early as 2023, Apple had already announced its subscription numbers had surpassed 1 billion. Reaching 1.5 billion nearly three years later is truly a remarkable achievement.

Apple's subscription services include its own services, such as Apple TV, Apple Music, iCloud+ and the Apple One bundle package.

However, it is widely expected that a large portion of these 1.5 billion subscriptions comes from App Store app subscriptions.

Whenever an iPhone, iPad or Mac user subscribes to a third-party app through the App Store, Apple takes a commission. Therefore, Apple is able to count these subscriptions in its total.
